
`lode doc edit` changes a document in place. For a plan this is the normal path at any status, and for a draft spec it is the body edit path. Both bump the version. For an accepted spec it is allowed only under the in-place amendment rules (WL-SPEC-77#sec-10a, WL-SPEC-77#sec-10b), with `--note` saying what changed or `--substantive`. `--if-version <n>` (`if_version` on the API) makes a body or column edit a compare-and-swap: the server compares `n` with the locked row's version and answers `409 Conflict` when they differ. Without it the edit overwrites. `lode doc link` and `lode doc unlink` write the document's outgoing edges: on a plan they are an edit and bump the version, on a draft spec they rewrite the live edges in place, and on an accepted spec they write the open candidate's edge set, opening a candidate if none is open (WL-SPEC-77#sec-3b). `lode doc edit --title` and `--issued` change the column without touching the body.
